title: Indoor Snow and Ski Centres: Skiing Without Mountains
description: Indoor real-snow centres for families: beginner ski and snowboard lessons, snow play and sledging, what to wear and how to prepare for a first ski holiday.
h1: Indoor snow centres: skiing without the mountains
intro: Real snow, all year round, often under an hour from home. Indoor snow centres are perfect for first-timers and for practising before a ski trip.

image.alt: People skating on an outdoor ice rink

cardText: Beginner lessons, snow play and what to wear.

blocks.title: Scout’s snow tip
blocks.text: Book a beginner lesson, not just slope time. You’ll learn to stop and turn safely, which is the bit that matters!
points: Snow play sessions suit little ones

sections.html: UK indoor real-snow centres include the Snowdome in Tamworth and Chill Factore in Manchester. Many areas also have outdoor dry slopes, which are cheaper but harder to fall on.

• Waterproof trousers and jacket.
  • Gloves (often compulsory) and warm layers.
  • Long socks. Boots, skis and helmets are usually provided with lessons.
A few lessons before a ski trip mean kids can join ski school at a higher level. Compare holidays on TravelDeals, and see snow and ice days out.

faqs.q: Can kids learn to ski indoors?
faqs.a: Yes. Indoor real-snow centres run children’s lessons, and some have snow play areas for younger kids not ready for skis.
